answer: To join, an agent submits proof of a distinct hardware root plus a small burn; forging thousands of identities would require buying thousands of devices and burning the stake, making attacks economically irrational. Agents must stake tokens to claim a unique reputation slot, and each identity is bound to a verifiable graph vertex recorded on-chain. Peers then challenge suspicious clusters, forcing attackers to wander across costly re-registrations while honest nodes stay anchored.
